entries.description: of Vanuatu have some fluency in Bislama
entries.subject: of Vanuatu

spans.text: Most of the population of the Republic of Vanuatu (estimated 218,000, July 2009) have some fluency in Bislama.

spans.text: Vanuatu is an archipelago of more than 80 islands located in the south-west Pacific.

entries.description: some Polynesian outliers in the central and southern islands
entries.subject: some Polynesian
entries.object: in the central and southern islands

spans.text: The c. 80–100 vernacular languages of Vanuatu mainly fall into the Eastern Oceanic family; there are some Polynesian outliers in the central and southern islands.

spans.text: Before that, it was jointly administered as a colony by both Britain and France (and was known then as the New Hebrides).

entries.description: that Vanuatu has been settled since c
entries.subject: that Vanuatu

spans.text: Archaeological evidence suggests that Vanuatu has been settled since c. 3200 BP.

entries.description: The region is characterized by extensive linguistic diversity
entries.subject: The region

spans.text: The region is characterized by extensive linguistic diversity; it is likely that during the history of Vanuatu some local languages have achieved lingua franca status in specific regions.

entries.description: Both scenarios are found in Vanuatu today
entries.subject: Both scenarios

spans.text: Both scenarios are found in Vanuatu today.

entries.task_id: with europeans|was|in 1606 with the voyage of pedro fernández de quirós
entries.description: with Europeans was in 1606 with the voyage of Pedro Fernández de Quirós
entries.subject: with Europeans
entries.object: in 1606 with the voyage of Pedro Fernández de Quirós

spans.text: First recorded contact of Ni-Vanuatu people with Europeans was in 1606 with the voyage of Pedro Fernández de Quirós, a Portuguese navigator who was sailing under a Spanish flag and who sent a boat ashore on Sakau Island off the north east coast.

entries.task_id: navigator who|was|sailing under a spanish flag and who sent a boat ashore on sakau island off the north east coast

spans.text: First recorded contact of Ni-Vanuatu people with Europeans was in 1606 with the voyage of Pedro Fernández de Quirós, a Portuguese navigator who was sailing under a Spanish flag and who sent a boat ashore on Sakau Island off the north east coast.

entries.task_id: this|is|what the islands were known as during the colonial period
entries.description: this is what the islands were known as during the colonial period
entries.subject: this
entries.object: what the islands were known as during the colonial period

spans.text: James Cook charted most of the Vanuatu archipelago in six weeks between 18 July and 31 August, 1772 and dubbed the islands the New Hebrides; this is what the islands were known as during the colonial period.

entries.task_id: language bislama|derives|its name
entries.description: language Bislama derives its name
entries.subject: language Bislama

spans.text: Much of the external trade during the early and mid-1800s was with whalers and traders from China including those interested in the biche de mer ‘sea cucumber’, from which the language Bislama derives its name.

entries.task_id: mainly what|is|now australia
entries.description: mainly what is now Australia
entries.subject: mainly what

spans.text: By the end of the 1860s, ships recruiting labourers for plantation work in the south-west Pacific (mainly what is now Australia, Fiji, New Caledonia, and Samoa) were frequenting the islands of Vanuatu.

the
practice

spans.text: Some labourers may have been effectively kidnapped, or “blackbirded” as the practice was known.

entries.description:

entries.subject:

entries.object: on the plantations in northern Queensland

spans.text: Workers on the plantations generally returned to Vanuatu after their contracts were up, and with them, they brought back material culture and the Pidgin English spoken on the plantations in northern Queensland.

entries.task_id: the bislama|spoken|today
entries.description: the Bislama spoken today
entries.subject: the Bislama

spans.text: This ultimately developed into the Bislama spoken today.

entries.task_id: bislama|carried|connotations of roughness or urban savvy
entries.description: Bislama carried connotations of roughness or urban savvy
entries.subject: Bislama
entries.object: connotations of roughness or urban savvy

spans.text: For many years, especially in outer islands, Bislama carried connotations of roughness or urban savvy; it could be seen as inappropriate for women to use the language.

entries.description: where it is the only L1 for many children
entries.subject: where it
entries.object: the only L1 for many children

spans.text: There has been some effort to introduce basic education in Bislama in the urban centres, where it is the only L1 for many children, but there is considerable resistance to this because many people still perceive it to be “bad English”.

entries.subject: New Testaments

spans.text: The Bible’s Old and New Testaments (with Psalms) have been translated into Bislama.

entries.description: translation team are effectively the only written standard
entries.subject: translation team

spans.text: The orthographic conventions used by the Bible translation team are effectively the only written standard, but there is considerable variability in how Bislama is written and spoken.

entries.subject: There
